name: France — French parties
intro: compare it with French political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of France: those represented in the National Assembly and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the National Assembly after the July 2024 legislative election (by parliamentary group), arranged left to right. Approximate. 577 members.

LFI.name: La France insoumise
LFI.ideologies: Democratic socialism, Left-wing populism, Eco-socialism, Soft Euroscepticism
LFI.priorities: Cost of living, Public services, Taxing wealth, Climate action, Democratic reform
LFI.description: Largest party of the French radical left, founded by Jean-Luc Mélenchon. It calls for a Sixth Republic, a higher minimum wage, retirement at 60, ecological planning and a break with EU budget rules.

PCF.name: Parti communiste français
PCF.priorities: Workers' rights and wages, Public services, Protecting national industry, Nuclear energy, Cost of living
PCF.description: One of France's oldest parties, with a base among workers and local councils. Unlike most of the left it defends nuclear power and industrial jobs, and it is critical of the EU's market rules.

PS.name: Parti socialiste
PS.priorities: Public services, Taxing wealth, Affordable housing, Climate action, Deeper European integration
PS.description: The historic party of the French centre-left, which governed under Mitterrand and Hollande. After years of decline it recovered in the 2024 European election and is part of the left alliance in the Assembly.

Écologistes.name: Les Écologistes
Écologistes.priorities: Climate action, Public services, Affordable housing, Civil liberties, Deeper European integration
Écologistes.description: France's main green party, formerly Europe Écologie Les Verts. It opposes new nuclear plants, supports a wealth tax and ambitious climate policy, and runs several large cities.

RE.name: Renaissance
RE.priorities: Competitiveness and growth, Deeper European integration, Defence and support for Ukraine, Nuclear energy, Education
RE.description: Emmanuel Macron's party, founded to break the left–right divide. Pro-business and strongly pro-European, it backed pension reform, nuclear power and European defence.

MoDem.name: Mouvement démocrate
MoDem.priorities: Fiscal discipline, Deeper European integration, Democratic reform, Education
MoDem.description: Centrist party led by François Bayrou, allied with Macron since 2017. It combines Christian-democratic roots with concern about public debt and support for proportional representation.

HOR.name: Horizons
HOR.priorities: Fiscal discipline, Security and law and order, Competitiveness and growth, Nuclear energy
HOR.description: Party of former prime minister Édouard Philippe, on the right of Macron's camp. It stresses fiscal discipline, security and state reform.

LR.name: Les Républicains
LR.priorities: Security and law and order, Reducing immigration, Fiscal discipline, Lower taxes, National identity
LR.description: The traditional Gaullist right of Chirac and Sarkozy. Weakened since 2017, it has taken a harder line on immigration and security while defending a market economy.

RN.name: Rassemblement national
RN.leader: Jordan Bardella (President), Marine Le Pen (Parliamentary leader)
RN.ideologies: National conservatism, Right-wing populism, Anti-immigration, Sovereignism
RN.priorities: Reducing immigration, Cost of living, Security and law and order, National sovereignty, Protecting national industry
RN.description: The largest single party in the National Assembly. It combines strict limits on immigration and 'national preference' with protectionist, welfare-friendly economics and opposition to further EU integration.

REC.name: Reconquête
REC.ideologies: Nationalism, National conservatism, Anti-immigration, Economic liberalism
REC.priorities: Remigration and closed borders, National identity, Lower taxes, Security and law and order, Traditional family values
REC.description: Party founded by the commentator Éric Zemmour. It is more economically liberal and more hard-line on immigration and identity than the RN.
